name: Schroedinger
notes: The starter: fastest Terran hull, fragile; a scout in Vega Strike

name: Franklin
notes: An Andolian diplomatic shuttle in Vega Strike; here the fleet's personnel transport (12 aboard). Usually escorted; the player flies it on one or two missions where nothing else can get through

name: Gawain
notes: High-Born main-line interceptor; confed_/highborn_/purist_ VDU liveries exist

name: Redeemer
notes: Aging Luddite in-system fighter flown by the border militias: thick armour, slug-throwers, no locking missiles

name: Pacifier
notes: Rear turret = a second human's seat (the gunner role the layer already has for WC2)

name: Lancelot
notes: Late-war heavy superiority fighter; in only if the art budget allows

name: Progeny
notes: Shaper craft: seldom met, usually the thing you escort (envoys, couriers)

name: Nicander
notes: Canon Aera interceptor

name: Ariston
notes: Canon Aera escort/superiority fighter

name: Areus
notes: Canon Aera assault craft

name: Agis
notes: NEW (tools/hulls.py AGIS): Nicander cut short, its wings swept sharply forward and lifted into a gull W; flown in swarms

name: Cleomenes
notes: NEW (hulls.py CLEOMEN): Areus thickened, with its own wing set upright above and below: a cross seen from the front

name: Convolution
notes: Vega Strike's Convolution (an Aera ship remade by Electrotech): asymmetric, so all 62 views. The aces' strike fighter: heavy energy guns and strafing runs, no missiles. In the Aera's teal sheen (data/art.csv). Took the place of the hulls.py Archidamus (the user's pick)

name: Shizu
notes: Rlaan reconnaissance; the Schroedinger's counterpart

name: Zhuangzong
notes: Rlaan mass-production fighter

name: Taizong
notes: Rlaan mass-production assault craft

name: Shizong
notes: Cripplers drain guns and engines: the Rlaan disable, they rarely kill

name: Xuanzong
notes: Unarmed in Vega Strike; here the interference itself: breaks locks and fills comms with static

name: Gaozong
notes: Rlaan probe: shadows every battle; shoot it or not, someone will remember

name: (asteroid field)
notes: Mission-ship type that registers a field (GameParams.asteroidField, as WC.EXE)

name: (mine field)
notes: GameParams.mineField

name: Vigilance
notes: The player's home, the TCS Vigilance: a Purist-built corvette of a mass-produced class that Vega Strike sends to the frontier against pirates and Aeran incursions; slow, tough and cheap, its one internal bay (the only one of its kind in Vega Strike's data) refitted as the wing's flight deck

name: Kahan
notes: Andolian torpedo destroyer: the trapped task force's backbone

name: Archimedes
notes: An aging Confed capital ship, formidable at long range (capital missiles more modern than itself, a refitted beam battery) while the rest of it shows its age: the task force's heavy hitter

name: Mule
notes: The most common hauler in human space

name: Ox
notes: Bulk convoys (Vega Strike's units.csv flies ox_new.bfxm)

name: Goddard
notes: Andolian heavy bomber, the Confederation's flying fortress (Vega Strike). Now and then a mission escorts one to its target; its turrets fight back

name: Watson
notes: Andolian and Mechanist support vessel, mostly automated: refuels and rearms small craft at docking clamps along its spine; the task force's tender, to be escorted, and a place to rearm

name: Clydesdale
notes: The only warship built in Merchant yards: a Confed workhorse with the task force (the player's home before the Vigilance)

name: Agasicles
notes: Venerable screening destroyer, nimble for its size

name: Anaxidamus
notes: Venerable cruiser with two fighter bays

name: Agesipolis
notes: Carrier on a scale of paranoid grandeur: half mobile base

name: Charillus
notes: Supply convoys; its tan livery needs repainting into Aera teal

name: Leonidas
notes: The finale; its VDU image is only a silhouette, so the art comes from the mesh

name: Ruizong
notes: Fast escort destroyer; weak shields, thick hide

name: Shundi
notes: Rlaan cruiser; launches the Rlaan fighters (Vega Strike has no Rlaan carrier)

name: Shenzong
notes: Rlaan cargo hauler; the salvage crews that follow every battle
